lynnwoodcitycenter.blurb: A major shared station on the 1 and 2 Lines in Snohomish County. Lynnwood City Center is a growing urban hub with a large transit-oriented development transforming the area around the station.
lynnwoodcitycenter.notableFact: The Lynnwood Link Extension added four new stations and brought light rail to Snohomish County for the first time.

mountlaketerrace.blurb: Serving the suburban community of Mountlake Terrace with a large park-and-ride facility. The station connects commuters to downtown Seattle in about 30 minutes.

shorelinenorth185th.blurb: Located at NE 185th Street alongside I-5 in Shoreline, this station serves the northern part of the city and has spurred significant transit-oriented development plans.

shorelinesouth148th.blurb: Serving southern Shoreline near NE 148th Street alongside I-5. The surrounding area is undergoing redevelopment with new housing and mixed-use projects.

pinehurst.blurb: An infill station at NE 130th Street serving the Pinehurst neighborhood between Shoreline and Northgate, currently under construction on the existing line.
pinehurst.notableFact: Pinehurst is the first infill station to be added to an operating Link line.

northgate.blurb: A major transit hub in the redeveloped Northgate Mall — now the Northgate Station district — with the Kraken Community Iceplex, the NHL team's three-rink practice house and headquarters, right next door. A pedestrian bridge links the station to North Seattle College.
northgate.notableFact: The John Lewis Memorial Bridge at Northgate spans I-5 to connect the station with North Seattle College.

roosevelt.blurb: A charming residential neighborhood with local restaurants and shops along Roosevelt Way. Named after President Theodore Roosevelt.

udistrict.blurb: The vibrant heart of Seattle's University District, steps from the Ave (University Way) with its eclectic mix of bookstores, restaurants, and student hangouts.
udistrict.notableFact: The U District station is over 90 feet deep, making it one of the deepest stations in the system.

universityofwashington.blurb: Located at the southeast edge of the UW campus near Husky Stadium. Provides direct access to one of the top research universities in the world.
universityofwashington.notableFact: This station opened as part of the University Link Extension in 2016, cutting the UW-to-downtown ride to under 10 minutes.

capitolhill.blurb: Seattle's most vibrant and eclectic neighborhood, known for its nightlife, diverse dining scene, and the iconic Pike/Pine corridor. Broadway threads south past Stoup Brewing's beer hall, the Himalayan basement Annapurna Cafe, and the plant-based bar Life on Mars. A cultural hub of the city.
capitolhill.notableFact: Capitol Hill station features 'Jet Kiss' by artist Mike Ross, two repurposed Navy jets suspended over the platform.

westlake.blurb: The bustling heart of downtown Seattle. Westlake is the system's busiest station, connecting to the Monorail, bus routes, and the retail core around Westlake Center and Pike Place Market.
westlake.notableFact: Westlake is the busiest Link station and serves as the downtown hub where the future 1, 2, and 3 Lines all converge.

symphony.blurb: Renamed from University Street to Symphony in 2024, this station serves Benaroya Hall, the Seattle Art Museum, and the downtown financial district.
symphony.notableFact: Renamed to Symphony to better reflect its proximity to Benaroya Hall, home of the Seattle Symphony.

pioneersquare.blurb: Seattle's original neighborhood, featuring historic red-brick buildings, art galleries, and the famous Underground Tour. The birthplace of the city.

internationaldistrictchinatown.blurb: A culturally rich neighborhood home to Seattle's Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese, and Filipino communities. The Wing Luke Museum and Uwajimaya grocery are neighborhood landmarks. Today's 2 Line trains branch east toward Judkins Park just south of here.
internationaldistrictchinatown.notableFact: This station is a major downtown transfer hub where the future 1, 2, and 3 Lines converge and the 2 Line branches east across Lake Washington.

stadium.blurb: Serving T-Mobile Park (Mariners) and Lumen Field (Seahawks/Sounders). The go-to station for Seattle's major sporting events and concerts.
stadium.notableFact: On game days, this station sees ridership spikes of up to 10x normal levels.

sodo.blurb: An industrial district south of downtown that's gradually evolving. SODO station provides access to the area's warehouses, breweries, and the Starbucks headquarters campus.
sodo.notableFact: The future West Seattle (3 Line) trains will branch off near SODO.

beaconhill.blurb: A diverse hilltop neighborhood with stunning views of downtown and Mount Rainier. Known for its community gardens, local restaurants, and the Jefferson Park golf course.
beaconhill.notableFact: Beacon Hill station is about 160 feet underground, making it the deepest station in the entire Link system.

mountbaker.blurb: A residential neighborhood with growing commercial activity along Rainier Avenue. The station connects to multiple bus routes serving the Rainier Valley.

columbiacity.blurb: One of Seattle's most diverse and beloved neighborhoods. Columbia City features a thriving main street with independent shops, restaurants from around the world, and a historic cinema.
columbiacity.notableFact: Columbia City was named one of the best neighborhoods in America by multiple publications for its diversity and walkability.

grahamstreet.blurb: A planned infill station between Columbia City and Othello, serving the Hillman City neighborhood. Part of a long-planned effort to improve transit access in the Rainier Valley.
grahamstreet.notableFact: Graham Street has been sought by the community since the original Link light rail opened in 2009.

othello.blurb: A multicultural neighborhood in the Rainier Valley with a mix of East African, Southeast Asian, and Latin American communities. Home to numerous ethnic grocery stores and restaurants.

rainierbeach.blurb: The southernmost Seattle neighborhood on the Link light rail. Rainier Beach is known for its community resilience, urban farm projects, and proximity to Lake Washington.

boeingaccessroad.blurb: A planned infill station between Rainier Beach and Tukwila, near Boeing's facilities along East Marginal Way. Will improve transit access to the Duwamish industrial area.

tukwilainternationalblvd.blurb: Serving the diverse Tukwila community along International Boulevard. The area is one of the most ethnically diverse zip codes in the United States.

seatacairport.blurb: Direct access to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport via a skybridge to the terminal. One of the most-used stations for visitors arriving in the region.
seatacairport.notableFact: SeaTac is one of the few US airports with direct light rail service to downtown, with a ride time of about 38 minutes.

anglelake.blurb: Named after the nearby Angle Lake, a popular swimming spot. The station includes a large parking garage and serves as a gateway to the southern suburbs.

kentdesmoines.blurb: Serving the communities of Kent and Des Moines along the Highway 99 corridor near Highline College. Part of the Federal Way Link Extension that brought rail further south.

starlake.blurb: A suburban station serving the Star Lake area between Kent and Federal Way. Features a park-and-ride facility for South King County commuters.

federalwaydowntown.blurb: The current southern terminus of the 1 Line. Federal Way Downtown station anchors the city's growing downtown core and connects to bus service throughout South King County.
federalwaydowntown.notableFact: The Federal Way Link Extension added 7.8 miles of light rail and three new stations in December 2025.

southfederalway.blurb: Planned station south of Federal Way Downtown, part of the Tacoma Dome Link Extension carrying the future 1 Line toward Tacoma.

fife.blurb: Planned station in the city of Fife along the Pacific Highway corridor, serving the growing communities between Federal Way and Tacoma.

easttacoma.blurb: Planned station near the Puyallup River and Portland Avenue, serving East Tacoma and the Puyallup Tribe's lands on the approach to the Tacoma Dome.

judkinspark.blurb: The first station east of the downtown tunnel, in the median of I-90 between Rainier Avenue S and 23rd Avenue S. Located in the diverse Judkins Park neighborhood of the Central District.
judkinspark.notableFact: Judkins Park opened in March 2026 with the Crosslake Connection, finally linking the Eastside 2 Line segment to Seattle.

mercerisland.blurb: Located in the median of I-90 between 77th and 80th avenues on the north end of Mercer Island, giving the island community a direct light rail connection to both Seattle and Bellevue.
mercerisland.notableFact: The 2 Line crosses Lake Washington on the I-90 floating bridge — the first light rail line on a floating bridge anywhere in the world.

southbellevue.blurb: An elevated station on Bellevue Way SE near Mercer Slough Nature Park, with a 1,500-stall park-and-ride garage serving Eastside commuters.

eastmain.blurb: Serving the residential areas of south-central Bellevue along 112th Avenue SE, near Surrey Downs Park and Old Bellevue with its boutique shopping district.

bellevuedowntown.blurb: The heart of the Eastside's largest city, at the east portal of the downtown Bellevue tunnel. Downtown Bellevue has transformed into a major urban center with gleaming high-rises, Bellevue Square, and a thriving restaurant scene.
bellevuedowntown.notableFact: Bellevue is the 5th largest city in Washington state and a major tech hub hosting Amazon, Meta, and other companies.

wilburton.blurb: An evolving neighborhood east of downtown Bellevue, home to the Bellevue Botanical Garden and the new Wilburton Village mixed-use development.

springdistrict.blurb: A brand-new neighborhood built around the station. The Spring District is home to a major Meta campus, the Global Innovation Exchange, and Bellevue Brewing's brewpub a block from the platform.
springdistrict.notableFact: The Spring District is one of the first neighborhoods in the region designed from the ground up around a light rail station.

belred.blurb: Formerly an industrial and auto-row corridor, Bel-Red is rapidly transforming into a mixed-use neighborhood with new apartments, shops, and creative spaces.

overlakevillage.blurb: Adjacent to the Microsoft campus area in Redmond. Overlake Village is a new urban center growing up around the station with housing, retail, and office space.

redmondtechnology.blurb: Serving the Redmond technology corridor including Microsoft and Nintendo of America. A major employment hub on the Eastside.
redmondtechnology.notableFact: Microsoft's main campus, adjacent to this station, employs tens of thousands of people.

marymoorvillage.blurb: Located along SR 520 near Marymoor Park, King County's largest park. The station includes a 1,400-stall park-and-ride garage and connects to regional trails.
marymoorvillage.notableFact: New King County trails connect Marymoor Village station directly to Marymoor Park and the regional trail network.

downtownredmond.blurb: The eastern terminus of the 2 Line, elevated along Cleveland Street in Redmond's walkable downtown. Saturday farmers markets and the Sammamish River Trail are steps away.
downtownredmond.notableFact: Redmond is known as the 'Bicycle Capital of the Northwest' with extensive trail connections from this station.

westalderwood.blurb: Planned station near Alderwood Mall on the Everett Link Extension, the first stop north of Lynnwood City Center.

ashway.blurb: Planned station near the existing Ash Way Park & Ride, serving south Snohomish County commuters on the shared 2/3 Line corridor.

mariner.blurb: Planned station near the existing Mariner Park & Ride. Under Sound Transit's future service plan, Mariner is the planned northern terminus of the 2 Line.

sr99airportroad.blurb: A provisional (unfunded) station on the Everett Link Extension at SR 99 and Airport Road, serving the surrounding commercial corridor.

sweverettindustrialcenter.blurb: Planned station near Paine Field and Boeing's Everett factory, the largest building in the world by volume. Will serve major aerospace manufacturing employment.
sweverettindustrialcenter.notableFact: The nearby Boeing Everett Factory is where the 747, 767, 777, and 787 Dreamliner were assembled.

sr526evergreen.blurb: Planned station near SR 526 and Evergreen Way on the Everett Link Extension, serving south Everett neighborhoods.

everettstation.blurb: The planned northern terminus of the future 3 Line at the existing Everett Station transit hub, connecting with Sounder commuter rail and Amtrak.
everettstation.notableFact: When complete, the Everett Link Extension will add 16 miles of light rail north of Lynnwood.

delridge.blurb: Planned station near Delridge Way and Andover Street in West Seattle. A diverse community with views of the Duwamish River valley.

avalon.blurb: Planned station near 35th Avenue SW and Avalon Way, providing a connection point between the Alaska Junction and Delridge communities.

alaskajunction.blurb: Planned terminus at the heart of West Seattle's Alaska Junction, the neighborhood's walkable village center with local shops and restaurants.
alaskajunction.notableFact: West Seattle was an independent city until it was annexed by Seattle in 1907, and many residents maintain a strong sense of separate identity.

southkirkland.blurb: Planned northern terminus of the future 4 Line at the existing South Kirkland Park & Ride, near the Cross Kirkland Corridor trail.

richardsroad.blurb: Planned elevated station on the north side of I-90 near Richards Road, serving the Factoria area of Bellevue.

eastgate.blurb: Planned station near the Eastgate Park & Ride and Bellevue College, a major transit connection point for the I-90 corridor.

lakemont.blurb: A provisional (unfunded) station near the Lakemont Boulevard interchange on I-90, between Eastgate and Issaquah in the Cascade foothills.

centralissaquah.blurb: Planned eastern terminus of the future 4 Line in Issaquah's regional growth center at the base of the Cascade foothills, gateway to Tiger Mountain trails and the historic downtown.
centralissaquah.notableFact: Issaquah hosts the annual Salmon Days festival celebrating the return of salmon to Issaquah Creek.

tacomadome.blurb: The eastern terminus of the T Line at the Tacoma Dome regional transit hub, connecting to Sounder commuter rail, Amtrak, and local buses. The future 1 Line from Seattle is planned to terminate here.
tacomadome.notableFact: The Tacoma Dome Link Extension is planned to bring 1 Line trains from Seattle to this station in 2035.

south25thstreet.blurb: Serving the residential neighborhoods south of downtown Tacoma near South 25th Street. One of the original T Line stations connecting Tacoma Dome to downtown.

unionstation.blurb: Located at Tacoma's beautifully restored Union Station, a Beaux-Arts landmark now housing a federal courthouse with Chihuly glass art installations in its grand hall.
unionstation.notableFact: Union Station features a permanent installation of Dale Chihuly glass art, free and open to the public.

conventioncenter.blurb: Serving the Greater Tacoma Convention Center and UW Tacoma campus. Located along Commerce Street above Tollefson Plaza.

theaterdistrict.blurb: A central T Line station in downtown Tacoma's Theater District. Near the Tacoma Art Museum, Museum of Glass, and the historic Pantages Theater.

oldcityhall.blurb: Station near Tacoma's historic Old City Hall, a Romanesque Revival landmark built in 1893. Part of the 2023 Hilltop Tacoma Link Extension.

s4th.blurb: Station along South 4th Street in downtown Tacoma, part of the Hilltop Extension providing access to the Stadium District area.

stadiumdistrict.blurb: Station in the Stadium District neighborhood, known for its historic Stadium High School featured in the film '10 Things I Hate About You.' The northernmost point on the T Line.
stadiumdistrict.notableFact: Stadium High School, near this station, was originally built as a luxury hotel in 1891 before being converted to a school.

tacomageneral.blurb: Station near MultiCare Tacoma General Hospital, part of the Hilltop Extension serving Tacoma's medical district.

6thavenue.blurb: Station along 6th Avenue near the Hilltop neighborhood, a vibrant commercial corridor with independent shops, restaurants, and galleries.

hilltopdistrict.blurb: A key T Line station in Tacoma's Hilltop neighborhood. The Hilltop Extension brought rail transit back to this historically underserved community.
hilltopdistrict.notableFact: The Hilltop Extension was a key equity project, reconnecting a neighborhood that lost its streetcar service in 1938.

stjoseph.blurb: The current western terminus of the T Line near St. Joseph Medical Center, on MLK Jr Way between South 17th and 19th streets.
stjoseph.notableFact: The T Line (originally Tacoma Link) was the first modern light rail line in the Puget Sound region, opening in 2003.

tacomacommunitycollege.blurb: The planned western terminus of a future T Line extension along the S 19th Street corridor to Tacoma Community College. Intermediate station locations have not been finalized.
